Fee-based accounts are legitimate and can hold stocks; the issue is whether the fee structure fits the customer.

questions.q: Two brothers own an account as joint tenants with right of survivorship (JTWROS). One brother dies. What happens to his share?
options: It passes to his estate under his will
It is split between his estate and his brother
It passes automatically to the surviving brother
The account is frozen until the IRS approves the transfer
questions.explain: With JTWROS, each owner has an undivided interest and the deceased owner's share passes directly to the surviving tenant, outside the estate. Passing the share to the estate is how tenants in common works, which is the common confusion. Firms still need documents such as a death certificate to retitle the account.

questions.q: Which statement about an account opened under the Uniform Transfers to Minors Act (UTMA) is accurate?
options: It may have two minors as beneficial owners
The custodian owns the assets for tax purposes
Gifts to the account can be taken back by the donor
Assets belong to the minor, there is one custodian and one minor, and the minor's Social Security number is used
questions.explain: An UTMA account has one custodian for one minor; gifts are irrevocable and the property belongs to the minor, whose Social Security number goes on the account. The custodian manages the assets for the minor's benefit until the age of transfer under state law, but does not own them.

questions.q: To open an account for a corporation, which document identifies the individuals authorized to trade on the corporation's behalf?
options: A corporate resolution
The corporation's annual report
The trust agreement
Form U4
questions.explain: A corporate resolution, adopted by the board, authorizes the account and names the officers who may give instructions. Margin accounts for corporations may also require a review of the charter to confirm margin borrowing is allowed. A trust agreement serves the same purpose for trust accounts, and Form U4 is for registered persons.

questions.q: Which statement about a Roth IRA is accurate?
options: Contributions are tax deductible, and all withdrawals are taxed
Qualified distributions, taken after the five-year period and after age 59½ (or another qualifying event), are tax free
The owner must start required minimum distributions at retirement
Roth IRAs can be opened only through an employer
questions.explain: Roth contributions are made with after-tax money, and qualified distributions, including earnings, are free of federal income tax. Unlike traditional IRAs, a Roth IRA does not require minimum distributions while the original owner is alive. Deductible contributions with taxable withdrawals describes a traditional IRA.

questions.q: A 45-year-old withdraws $20,000 from a traditional IRA funded entirely with deductible contributions, for a purpose not covered by any exception. What is the federal tax consequence?
options: No tax, because IRAs are tax deferred
Capital gains tax on the growth only
Ordinary income tax on $20,000 plus a 10% additional tax of $2,000
A 10% additional tax only, with no income tax
questions.explain: Distributions of deductible contributions and earnings from a traditional IRA are taxed as ordinary income, and withdrawals before age 59½ generally also trigger a 10% additional tax unless an exception applies. Here that is ordinary income on $20,000 plus $2,000. IRA withdrawals are never taxed as capital gains.

questions.q: An employee receives a check for her 401(k) balance when she changes jobs and wants to roll it into an IRA. Which statement is accurate?
options: She has 60 days to complete the rollover, and the plan must have withheld 20% for federal tax
She has 12 months to complete the rollover with no withholding
A rollover is not allowed from a 401(k) to an IRA
She must pay a 10% additional tax even if she rolls it over in time
questions.explain: An indirect rollover must be completed within 60 days, and plans must withhold 20% from eligible rollover distributions paid to the participant; to roll over the full amount she must replace the withheld 20% from other funds. A direct trustee-to-trustee rollover avoids withholding. Completed rollovers are not taxed or penalized.

questions.q: What is the purpose of required minimum distributions (RMDs) from traditional IRAs and most employer plans?
options: To ensure tax-deferred retirement savings are eventually withdrawn and taxed
To limit how much a person may contribute each year
To prevent withdrawals before retirement
To pay plan administration fees
questions.explain: RMD rules require owners of tax-deferred accounts to start withdrawing a minimum amount each year once they reach the age set by law, so the deferred tax is eventually collected. Failing to take an RMD can lead to an excise tax. Contribution limits and early-withdrawal rules are separate parts of the tax code.

questions.q: A criminal moves illegal cash through a series of wire transfers among accounts in several countries to obscure where it came from. Which stage of money laundering is this?
options: Placement
Integration
Structuring
Layering
questions.explain: Layering uses multiple transactions to separate funds from their criminal source and make them hard to trace. Placement is the first entry of cash into the financial system, and integration is the final stage, when the cleaned money returns to the legitimate economy, for example as an investment. Structuring is a technique for avoiding reports at placement.

questions.q: A customer deposits $9,500 in currency on Monday, $9,000 on Tuesday and $9,800 on Wednesday, each time asking whether the amount will be reported. What should the firm do?
options: Nothing, because no single deposit exceeded $10,000
Tell the customer to combine the deposits so a CTR is filed
Evaluate the pattern as possible structuring and file a SAR if it is suspicious, without telling the customer
Close the account and inform the customer that a report was filed
questions.explain: Breaking up cash deposits to avoid the over-$10,000 currency transaction report is structuring, a crime itself. The pattern and questions about reporting are red flags, so the firm should escalate and file a Suspicious Activity Report if warranted. Firms may never tell a customer that a SAR has been or will be filed.

questions.q: A broker-dealer must file a Currency Transaction Report (CTR) with FinCEN when a customer:
options: deposits more than $10,000 in currency in one business day
wires any amount to a foreign country
buys more than $10,000 of stock with a personal check
opens an account with a foreign passport
questions.explain: CTRs cover transactions in currency (cash) of more than $10,000 in a business day, including multiple cash transactions that add up. Checks and wires are not currency, though they can still be suspicious. Account opening with foreign identification falls under the customer identification program, not CTR rules.

questions.q: Under FinCEN rules, a broker-dealer that detects a suspicious transaction of at least $5,000 generally must file a SAR within how many calendar days of initial detection?
questions.explain: A broker-dealer must file a SAR no later than 30 calendar days after first detecting facts that may require one; if no suspect is identified, it may take up to 30 more days, but never more than 60 days in total. Supporting documents must be kept for five years.

questions.q: Before opening an account, a firm finds that the prospective customer's name matches an entry on OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list. What should the firm do?
options: Open the account but limit it to cash purchases
Not open the account, block any property as required and report to OFAC
Open the account after the customer signs a statement of innocence
Ask FINRA for permission to open the account
questions.explain: U.S. persons, including broker-dealers, may not do business with SDNs; property of a confirmed match must be blocked and the firm must report to OFAC. Possible matches should be checked to confirm the identity before acting. FINRA cannot grant permission to deal with sanctioned persons.
questions.rule: Office of Foreign Assets Control regulations

questions.q: Under a broker-dealer's customer identification program (CIP), what minimum information must generally be collected from an individual before opening an account?
options: Name, date of birth, address and an identification number such as a Social Security number
Name and phone number only
Name, employer and annual income only
A credit report and two bank references
questions.explain: Section 326 of the USA PATRIOT Act and the CIP rule require name, date of birth, residential or business street address, and an identification number (a taxpayer ID for U.S. persons). The firm must then verify identity within a reasonable time. Income and employer information are suitability (KYC) data, not CIP minimums.

questions.q: Under SEC Rule 17a-4, records such as the firm's blotters and general ledgers must be kept for at least how long?
options: Three years, the first year easily accessible
Four years
Six years, the first two years in an easily accessible place
Permanently
questions.explain: Rule 17a-4 requires blotters, ledgers and certain other core records to be preserved for at least six years, the first two in an easily accessible place. Many other records, such as order tickets and communications, must be kept for at least three years. Four years applies to FINRA's written complaint records.

questions.q: When must a broker-dealer send a customer a confirmation of a securities transaction?
options: At or before the completion of the transaction
Within 30 days of the trade
Only at the end of the quarter, on the account statement
Only if the customer requests it
questions.explain: FINRA Rule 2232 and SEC Rule 10b-10 require a written confirmation at or before completion of the transaction, which in practice means no later than settlement. Account statements are separate and are sent at least quarterly under Rule 2231.

questions.q: How often must a general securities member send account statements to a customer whose account had a security position, money balance or activity during the period?
options: Monthly
Annually
Only when there is trading activity
At least once each calendar quarter
questions.explain: FINRA Rule 2231 requires account statements at least once every calendar quarter showing positions, money balances and account activity. Many firms send monthly statements when there is activity, but the rule's minimum is quarterly, so monthly is a firm practice, not the requirement.

questions.q: A customer leaving on a long trip asks the firm to hold her mail. Under FINRA Rule 3150, which is accurate?
options: Firms may never hold customer mail
The firm may hold mail on written instructions; a request longer than three consecutive months must include an acceptable reason other than convenience
The firm may hold mail on the representative's verbal request
The firm must forward the mail to the representative's home
questions.explain: Rule 3150 allows a firm to hold mail on the customer's written instructions, after telling the customer about other ways to monitor the account such as email or the website. Holds longer than three consecutive months need an acceptable reason such as safety, and convenience is not enough. The firm must also be able to show it is not hiding activity.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a broker-dealer's business continuity plan (BCP) under FINRA Rule 4370?
options: To set sales targets for the coming year
To explain the firm's commission schedule
To let the firm meet its obligations to customers during a significant business disruption
To describe the firm's arbitration procedures
questions.explain: Rule 4370 requires firms to create, maintain and review a plan for responding to emergencies or disruptions, covering items such as data backup, alternate communications and how customers can reach the firm. A summary must be disclosed to customers at account opening and posted on the firm's website.

questions.q: Under Regulation S-P, a broker-dealer that wants to share a customer's nonpublic personal information with a nonaffiliated third party for marketing must generally:
options: share it freely, since the customer opened an account
obtain written consent from FINRA
delete the information after sharing
give the customer a privacy notice and a reasonable opportunity to opt out first
questions.explain: Regulation S-P requires an initial privacy notice when the relationship starts and a chance to opt out before nonpublic personal information is shared with nonaffiliated third parties, subject to exceptions such as servicing the account. Firms must also maintain written policies to safeguard customer information.

questions.q: A registered representative emails the same market commentary to 40 retail investors over two weeks. Under FINRA Rule 2210, this is a:
options: retail communication
piece of correspondence
institutional communication
private communication exempt from supervision
questions.explain: Written communications distributed to more than 25 retail investors within any 30 calendar-day period are retail communications, which generally need principal approval before use. Correspondence is limited to 25 or fewer retail investors in that period. The 40 recipients over two weeks put this over the line.

questions.q: Under FINRA's telemarketing rule, a representative may not make an outbound sales call to a person's home, unless an exception applies, at what times?
options: Before 9 a.m. or after 5 p.m. of the caller's time zone
Before 8 a.m. or after 9 p.m. local time at the called person's location
On weekends only
Before noon on business days
questions.explain: Rule 3230 bars calls to a residence before 8 a.m. or after 9 p.m. local time of the called party, unless there is an established business relationship, prior consent, or the person is a broker-dealer. The local time of the person called, not the caller, controls. Firms must also honor do-not-call lists.

questions.q: A person tells a representative during a cold call not to call again. What must the firm do?
options: Nothing, unless the person is on the national do-not-call registry
Stop calling for one week
Add the person to the firm's own do-not-call list and honor the request
Transfer the person to another representative
questions.explain: Firms must keep a firm-specific do-not-call list and honor requests made directly to them, regardless of whether the person is on the national registry. The national registry is a separate obligation, so the first choice understates the duty.

questions.q: Under Regulation Best Interest, when does the care obligation apply?
options: Whenever a broker-dealer recommends a securities transaction or investment strategy to a retail customer
Only when the customer pays a commission above 5%
Only for discretionary accounts
Only after the customer complains
questions.explain: Reg BI applies when a broker-dealer or its associated person makes a recommendation of a securities transaction or strategy, including account type recommendations, to a retail customer. The firm must act in the customer's best interest without placing its own interest ahead. It is triggered by the recommendation, not by fees or complaints.

questions.q: FINRA Rule 2090 (Know Your Customer) requires firms to use reasonable diligence to know the essential facts about a customer:
options: only when the customer first buys an IPO
only for customers with margin accounts
only if the customer has more than $1 million in assets
at account opening and throughout the relationship
questions.explain: Rule 2090 applies when the account is opened and for as long as it is maintained, regardless of whether a recommendation is made. Essential facts include those needed to service the account, follow special handling instructions and know who has authority to act. Suitability (Rule 2111) adds investment profile duties when recommending.

questions.q: A representative learns that the firm is about to execute a large customer block sale of XYZ and sells XYZ in his own account first. This is:
options: front running, a prohibited practice
best execution
legitimate hedging
an allowed principal trade
questions.explain: Trading ahead of a known pending block order to profit from its expected price effect is front running, prohibited under FINRA Rule 5270. It exploits customer order information that the firm should hold in confidence. Hedging does not excuse trading on nonpublic knowledge of an imminent block.

questions.q: A trader places a series of buy orders in the final minutes of trading to push a stock's closing price higher, improving the value of positions held. This is:
options: backing away
marking the close
trading ahead
freeriding
questions.explain: Marking the close means placing trades near the end of the session to influence the closing price, which is manipulative. Backing away is a market maker's failure to honor its firm quote. Freeriding is buying and selling in a cash account without paying for the purchase.

questions.q: A group spreads false positive rumors online about a thinly traded stock it owns and sells into the resulting price spike. This scheme is called:
options: arbitrage
a wash sale
a pump and dump
dollar-cost averaging
questions.explain: In a pump and dump, promoters inflate the price with false or misleading claims, then sell their shares at the inflated price, leaving other investors with losses. It is fraudulent market manipulation. A wash sale in the tax sense is buying back substantially identical securities around a loss sale, a different issue.

questions.q: A customer buys stock in a cash account, then sells it before paying for the purchase, using the sale proceeds to pay. What is the consequence under Regulation T?
options: None; this is normal day trading
The customer is barred from trading for life
The firm must convert the account to a margin account
The account is frozen for 90 calendar days, during which purchases must be paid for in full in advance
questions.explain: Selling an unpaid purchase in a cash account is freeriding. Regulation T then withdraws the privilege of delayed payment for 90 calendar days, so the customer must have funds in the account before buying. The other choices invent consequences that the regulation does not impose.

questions.q: A company's CFO tells her brother that quarterly earnings will badly miss forecasts before the news is public, and the brother sells his shares. Who may be liable for insider trading?
options: Only the brother, because he traded
Only the CFO, because she had the information
Both the CFO as tipper and the brother as tippee
Neither, because they are family members
questions.explain: Insider trading liability covers anyone who trades on material nonpublic information in breach of a duty, and also the person who tips it. The CFO breached her duty by tipping, and the brother knew the information came from an insider. Family relationships do not shield either; Rule 10b5-2 even treats close family as having duties of trust.

questions.q: In an SEC civil action for insider trading, the court may impose a penalty on the person who traded of up to:
options: three times the profit gained or loss avoided
the amount of profit gained only
$5,000 per trade
ten times the profit gained
questions.explain: Section 21A of the Exchange Act, added by ITSFEA, allows civil penalties up to three times the profit gained or loss avoided, in addition to disgorgement. Controlling persons who fail to prevent violations can face separate penalties, and criminal prosecution can bring fines and prison.

questions.q: A registered representative wants to buy shares of a hot equity IPO for her own account. Under FINRA Rule 5130, what is the general rule?
options: She may buy any amount if she pays the offering price
She may buy if her branch manager approves
She may buy only through another firm
As a restricted person, she generally may not buy new issue equity shares
questions.explain: Rule 5130 prohibits member firms from selling new issues to restricted persons, a category that includes broker-dealer personnel and certain family members, so the public offering is not diverted to insiders. Approval by a manager or using another firm does not change her restricted status.

questions.q: A representative's longtime customer, who is not a relative or a lending institution, offers him a personal loan. Under FINRA Rule 3240, which is required?
options: Nothing; loans between friends are private
The arrangement must fit the firm's written procedures allowing such loans, with notice to and approval by the firm as required
Only the customer's written consent
A Form U5 filing
questions.explain: Borrowing from or lending to customers is prohibited unless the firm has written procedures allowing it and the arrangement falls into a permitted category, such as immediate family or a personal relationship outside the broker-customer relationship, with notification and approval as the rule requires. Treating it as purely private is the trap.

questions.q: A representative tells a customer: if this stock loses money, I will personally cover your loss. Under FINRA Rule 2150, this is:
options: allowed with written disclosure
allowed for accredited investors
prohibited, because guaranteeing a customer against loss is not permitted
allowed if a principal signs off
questions.explain: Rule 2150 forbids members and associated persons from guaranteeing a customer against loss in a securities transaction or account. Sharing in profits and losses is allowed only in a joint account with the firm's written approval and generally in proportion to the representative's contribution, which is a different situation.

questions.q: Under FINRA Rule 2165, which customer is a specified adult?
options: Any customer with a trusted contact person
Any customer aged 60 or older
Any customer with a margin account
A customer aged 65 or older, or aged 18 or older whom the firm reasonably believes has an impairment preventing self-protection
questions.explain: Rule 2165 defines a specified adult as a natural person 65 or older, or 18 or older with a mental or physical impairment that makes the person unable to protect his or her own interests. It lets firms place temporary holds on disbursements when financial exploitation is reasonably suspected.

questions.q: A broker-dealer pays a referral fee, based on transactions, to an unregistered accountant who sends it brokerage customers. This violates which principle?
options: Members may not pay transaction-based compensation to unregistered persons
Members may not accept referrals from accountants
Accountants must register with the MSRB
No rule is violated if the fee is disclosed
questions.explain: FINRA Rule 2040 bars members from paying transaction-based compensation to persons who would have to be registered as broker-dealers or associated persons to receive it. Disclosure does not cure the problem. Accepting referrals is fine; paying the unregistered person per transaction is the issue.

questions.q: A representative has a customer sign several blank account forms so he can fill them in later. This practice:
options: is acceptable if the customer trusts him
creates signatures of convenience and is a prohibited falsification risk
is required for discretionary accounts
is allowed if the forms are kept in the branch
questions.explain: Using pre-signed blank forms or signing for a customer, even with permission, creates documents that do not reflect what the customer actually approved; FINRA treats these signatures of convenience as falsifying records and a violation of high standards of commercial honor under Rule 2010.

questions.q: Which activity may an unregistered assistant at a broker-dealer perform?
options: Accept customer orders while the representative is out
Recommend mutual funds to customers
Solicit new accounts by cold calling and discussing specific stocks
Schedule appointments and handle clerical tasks without discussing investments
questions.explain: Unregistered persons may do clerical and administrative work, such as scheduling and filing, but may not accept orders, recommend securities or solicit securities business. Taking orders when the representative is away is a classic violation, because order taking is a registered function.

questions.q: Which event can cause a statutory disqualification from association with a FINRA member?
options: A personal bankruptcy filing
A felony conviction within the past ten years
Failing the SIE exam
A customer complaint that was settled for less than $5,000
questions.explain: Under Section 3(a)(39) of the Exchange Act, statutory disqualification includes certain felony convictions within ten years, certain misdemeanors involving securities or dishonesty, and regulatory bars. A bankruptcy must be disclosed on Form U4 but does not by itself disqualify a person. Failing an exam simply means no registration yet.

questions.q: Why does a broker-dealer submit fingerprints of its associated persons?
options: So the FBI can check criminal history records as part of the background check
To register the person with the IRS
To verify the person's exam scores
Fingerprinting is optional for all employees
questions.explain: SEC Rule 17f-2 requires fingerprinting of most broker-dealer personnel, and the prints are submitted for an FBI criminal history check. Together with the Form U4 review, this lets the firm and FINRA identify disqualifying history. It has nothing to do with the IRS or exam results.

questions.q: A person passes the SIE exam but has not yet passed a representative-level exam or been registered through a member firm. Which is accurate?
options: She may sell securities of any kind
She may sell only mutual funds
She may not act as a registered representative until she passes the qualification exam and is registered through a member firm
She may supervise registered representatives
questions.explain: The SIE is a general knowledge co-requisite exam; passing it alone does not qualify anyone to register. A person must also pass the appropriate representative exam, such as the Series 6 or Series 7, and be registered through a FINRA member firm before doing business as a representative.

questions.q: What is the difference between the Regulatory Element and the Firm Element of FINRA continuing education?
options: Regulatory Element content comes from FINRA and covers rules and regulatory topics; Firm Element training is designed by each firm for its own registered persons
Both are designed by the firm
Firm Element is required only for principals
Regulatory Element is optional
questions.explain: Under FINRA Rule 1240, the Regulatory Element is FINRA-delivered training on regulatory and compliance topics that registered persons must complete, while the Firm Element is a training program each firm develops based on its own business, products and needs assessment. Neither element is optional for covered persons.

questions.q: A registered representative is charged with a felony. How soon must his Form U4 be amended?
options: Within 10 days
Only after a conviction
Within 30 days of learning of the charge
At the next annual renewal
questions.explain: Form U4 must be kept current, and amendments are due no later than 30 days after learning of the facts that require them. Felony charges are reportable when filed, not only after conviction, which is the trap in the second choice.

questions.q: A firm terminates a representative's employment. Which form must it file, and when?
options: Form U4, within 10 days
Form U5, within 30 days of termination, with a copy to the individual
Form BD, within 60 days
No form; FINRA learns of terminations automatically
questions.explain: The firm must file Form U5 within 30 days of terminating an associated person's registration and provide a copy to the individual; amendments are due within 30 days of learning new facts. Form U4 is for registration and updates, and Form BD is the broker-dealer's own registration form.

questions.q: What is the consequence of knowingly filing misleading information on Form U4?
options: None, if it is corrected later
Only a written warning
Automatic loss of the SIE exam result
It violates FINRA rules and can lead to sanctions, including a bar, and may be a statutory disqualification
questions.explain: FINRA Rule 1122 prohibits filing incomplete or inaccurate registration information that is misleading, and willful misstatements on Form U4 can lead to fines, suspension, a bar and statutory disqualification. A later correction does not erase the original violation.

questions.q: Under FINRA Rule 4513, how long must a member keep records of written customer complaints at the office of supervisory jurisdiction?
options: One year
Two years
At least four years
Ten years
questions.explain: Rule 4513 requires each member to keep a record of every written customer complaint for at least four years, including the complainant's name, the date, the action taken and related correspondence. The four-year figure is specific to complaints and differs from the three- and six-year periods in SEC Rule 17a-4.

questions.q: Which situation is a red flag that a supervisor should investigate?
options: A representative's customer has a trusted contact person on file
A customer receives quarterly statements
A representative has an outside activity disclosed and approved
A representative asks that a customer's statements be sent to the representative's home
questions.explain: Redirecting customer mail to a representative's address can hide unauthorized trading or theft and is a well-known warning sign. Trusted contacts, approved outside activities and regular statements are signs of proper procedure, not problems.

questions.q: A registered representative wants to work weekends as a paid real estate agent. Under FINRA Rule 3270, what must she do?
options: Nothing, because real estate is not securities business
Give her firm prior written notice before starting
Get approval from the SEC
Resign her registration
questions.explain: Rule 3270 requires registered persons to provide prior written notice to their firm before engaging in outside business activities for compensation, so the firm can assess conflicts and decide whether to restrict them. That the activity involves no securities does not remove the notice duty.

questions.q: A representative wants to help a friend's startup sell its private shares to investors and will receive a fee. Under FINRA Rule 3280, what is required?
options: Nothing, because the shares are private
Only verbal notice to the branch manager
Written notice to the firm in advance, and the firm's written approval; the firm must then record and supervise the transactions
Registration of the startup with FINRA
questions.explain: Rule 3280 covers private securities transactions outside the regular course of employment. Before taking part, the person must give written notice describing the deal and his role; if he is compensated, the firm must approve or disapprove in writing, and an approved transaction must be recorded and supervised as if it were the firm's own.

questions.q: Under MSRB Rule G-37, a municipal finance professional who is entitled to vote for an issuer official may contribute, without triggering a business ban, up to:
options: $250 per election to that official
$1,000 per year to that official
Any amount if it is reported
Nothing at all under any circumstances
questions.explain: Rule G-37 exempts contributions of up to $250 per election by a municipal finance professional to an official he or she is entitled to vote for. Larger contributions can bar the dealer from municipal securities business with that issuer for two years. Simply reporting a contribution does not avoid the ban.

questions.q: A dealer's municipal finance professional makes a contribution that is not exempt under MSRB Rule G-37 to an official of a city. What is the result?
options: The professional is fined but the firm is unaffected
The city must refuse future bond issues
The dealer is generally banned from municipal securities business with that city for two years
The contribution must be returned within one year
questions.explain: A contribution that exceeds the de minimis exemption generally bars the dealer from engaging in municipal securities business with that issuer for two years. This pay-to-play rule targets the firm's business, which is why the first choice is wrong. Prompt return of a small contribution may support exemptive relief, but it is not automatic.

questions.q: A representative takes a client's employee, who manages the client's brokerage business, to a sporting event and attends with him. Under FINRA rules, this is generally treated as:
options: a gift subject to the annual gift limit
business entertainment, permitted if it is not so frequent or extensive as to raise questions of propriety, under the firm's procedures
a prohibited payment in all cases
non-cash compensation that must be filed with FINRA
questions.explain: When the representative attends with the guest, the event is business entertainment rather than a gift. It is allowed if it is reasonable and not so frequent or extensive as to raise questions of propriety, and firms must have written policies to supervise it. If the representative simply gave away the tickets, it would be treated as a gift.

questions.q: Which of the following must be disclosed on a registered representative's Form U4?
options: A personal bankruptcy filing
A parking ticket
A change in marital status
A home purchase
questions.explain: Form U4 asks about bankruptcies, unsatisfied liens and judgments, criminal charges and convictions, regulatory actions, customer complaints and terminations. Minor traffic offenses, marriage and home purchases are not reportable events. A bankruptcy filing does not bar the person but must be disclosed.

questions.q: Under FINRA Rule 4530, a member must report specified events, such as certain written customer complaints alleging theft or a person being subject to a regulatory action, within how many calendar days after it knows or should have known?
questions.explain: Rule 4530(a) requires prompt reporting to FINRA, and in any event no later than 30 calendar days after the firm knows or should have known of the event. Separately, firms report statistical summaries of customer complaints quarterly, by the 15th day of the month after each calendar quarter.

questions.q: FINRA's BrokerCheck is primarily a tool that:
options: executes customer trades at the best price
lets the public research the background and registration history of firms and individuals
calculates margin requirements
replaces Form U4
questions.explain: BrokerCheck draws on registration data, largely from Forms U4, U5 and BD, to show employment history, registrations and disclosure events such as customer complaints and regulatory actions. Firms must include a reference to BrokerCheck on their websites and in some communications.
